## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The reset and signup validators now require twelve characters, and their tests check the 11/12 boundary. The PR still needs one fix before merge. The PR body says the change raises the minimum "in the password validators", but the invite validator still accepts eight characters, so the new policy is only partly enforced.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/signup.py:1 — correctness — This PR raises `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` to 12 in `app/signup.py` and `app/reset.py` but leaves `app/invite.py:1` at `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8`. Its `accepts_password` therefore still accepts a password like `"x" * 8` (or any 8–11 character password) that signup and reset now reject. `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` still asserts the old `length >= 8` rule. Could you raise `app/invite.py:1` to 12 and update `tests/test_invite.py` to use the same `[0, 8, 11, 12, 13]` / `length >= 12` cases as the other two tests? Alternatively, move the constant into one shared module so the three validators can't drift apart again. — Accounts created through the invite flow can still get passwords of 8–11 characters, which breaks the twelve-character security policy this PR says it enforces.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_reset.py:6-8` and `tests/test_signup.py:6-8` test lengths 11, 12 and 13 against the new rule. A mistake that kept the old value or turned `>=` into `>` in either changed validator would make these tests fail.
